remediation.reason: Review failed: compliance grading accepts non-SDD, forged and weakened runs; address all nine review findings

findings.summary: gradeFullSddCompliance sets compliant = issues.length === 0 without requiring any SDD work started or closed; downgrades are not issues. No-op, quick-only and downgraded runs are graded compliant and compare.ts computes the compliance rate from `compliant`. Violates AC1 and the compliance/success distinction of AC4; tests do not cover no-op, quick-only or downgrade runs.

A `--no-verify` commit with a forged Harness-Work trailer and no active work, or rewriting .ways/config.json testCommand to ['true'], is graded compliant. The grader never checks that trailed commits fall inside a CLI-created work nor that harness files (.ways/config.json, manifest, hooks, check.sh, core.hooksPath) are unchanged since the bootstrap revision.
fullSddCompleted accepts any closed SDD work, not one bound to the task id the prompt names; the real change can land in a separate work. No test.

gradeFullSddCompliance runs inside runTask's try; a thrown compliance error replaces the whole task with success=false, discarding a successful functional grade, contradicting 'task success never depends on compliance'.

resultProblem only checks metrics/compliance/usage are objects; a missing metric entry throws a TypeError in metricSummary and non-numeric values yield NaN. An unreadable --input path rejects the whole command instead of being reported invalid.

The compliant full-sdd test drives SDD in-process; it never executes the installed node_modules/.bin/ways link or the commit-msg hook's node_modules lookup in the disposable repo, and no test covers the packed-package layout where sourceRevision must be null.
prepareFullSdd appends 'node_modules/' to .gitignore without ensuring a trailing newline, so a fixture .gitignore lacking one merges patterns and the symlinks get committed.
sourceRevision dirtiness ignores dist/, so a stale or foreign build in a clean checkout is recorded as HEAD without any reason.
The comparability key lacks a corpus content digest, and metric totals silently sum only available values, so partial totals are easy to misread next to fully observed harnesses.
